question: to the Commission Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Özlem Demirel (The Left), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Hana Jalloul Muro (S&D), Ciaran Mullooly (Renew), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Estrella Galán (The Left), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Catarina Martins (The Left), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE), Marc Botenga (The Left), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Martin Sonneborn (NI), Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Sibylle Berg (NI), Emma Fourreau (The Left), Kathleen Funchion (The Left), Branislav Ondruš (NI), Danilo Della Valle (The Left) Subject:

The German state is prosecuting five European citizens before the higher regional court in Stuttgart in proceedings marked by procedural irregularities: the accused appear in court handcuffed and confined to a glass cage, despite having no criminal records or prior disciplinary incidents; the trial is being held in a special courtroom, surrounded by barbed wire; the presiding judge has repeatedly rejected defence arguments without giving reasons; and the accused have been held in pre-trial detention for months for acts limited to property damage. The European Court of Human Rights established in Svinarenko and Slyadnev v Russia1 that confinement in restraint structures during trial constitutes degrading treatment under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), and in Jiga v Romania2 that presenting accused persons in handcuffs without individual justification violates Article 6(2). The fact that the accused are being prosecuted for opposing an Israeli defence company’s operations in Gaza compounds these concerns and points to proceedings bearing the hallmarks of political persecution. 1.
Are the procedural conditions described compatible with Article 47 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and Directive 2016/343/EU3?
If not, does the Commission intend to open a formal dialogue with German authorities regarding compliance with these guarantees?

Judgment of the European Court of Human Rights of 17 July 2014, Svinarenko and Slyadnev v Russia, application nos 32541/08 and 43441/08. 2 Judgment of the European Court of Human Rights of 16 March 2010, Jiga v Romania, application no 14352/04. 3 Directive (EU) 2016/343 of 9 March 2016 on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2016/343/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.9.2026) The Commission places great importance on ensuring respect for the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. Directive (EU) 2016/3431, which contributes to safeguarding the right to a fair trial and the rights of defence set out in Article 6 of the European Convention of Human Rights and in Articles 47 and 48 the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU, requires Member States to ensure that suspects or accused persons are not presented as being guilty, whether in court or in public, through the use of measures of physical restraint. Such measures may only be used where justified by case-specific reasons, relating to security or to the prevention of suspects or accused persons from absconding or from having contact with third persons. The Commission is closely monitoring the transposition and application of this Directive. Where specific non-conformity issues arise, the Commission will take every appropriate measure to ensure the compliance of national legislation with the Directive. Detention issues fall primarily within the responsibility of the Member States. On 8 December 2022, the Commission adopted the Recommendation on the procedural rights of suspects and accused in pre-trial detention and on material detention conditions2. By the end of 2026, the Commission will publish a report assessing the national measures taken by the Member States to implement the Recommendation.
1 Directive (EU) 2016/343 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on the strengthening

of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings, OJ L 65, 11.3.2016, pp. 1–11. 2 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/681 of 8 December 2022 on procedural rights of suspects and accused persons subject to pre-trial detention and on material detention conditions, C/2022/8987, OJ L 86, 24.3.2023, p. 44–57.
